intro_html: King Ranch chicken is a Texas classic, all cheesy, saucy comfort in one pot. This meal prep version keeps the flavor, stacks up the protein, and stays cheap per serving. One batch makes 14 servings.
cost_closing_html: About $3.76 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 servings comes in around 60g protein for about 567 calories, at roughly $2.16 a bowl.
upsell_html: Cheesy, comforting, and cheap, this bowl proves meal prep does not have to taste like a diet. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Buy the cheddar in the bigger two-bag size. It is cheaper per ounce and this recipe puts it to good use.
Reach for the bulk chicken breast to keep the per serving price low.
A single can of diced tomatoes is all the sauce base you need, so no pricey extras here.
make_it: Set the chicken breast in the crock with the can of diced tomatoes.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours until the chicken shreds easily.
Shred the chicken and stir it back into the sauce.
Stir in most of the cheddar and let it melt through.
Steam the broccoli and cook the rice.
Build bowls with rice, king ranch chicken, broccoli, and the last of the cheese on top.

head.description: A high-protein Tex-Mex meal prep. Fourteen servings at about 567 calories and 60 grams of protein for roughly $3.76 each (at everyday cost).
